title: Morning Robotics Scan
report:
## WarpWeaver: Decentralized Real‑Time Multi‑Robot Planner

### The Breakthrough
WarpWeaver is a decentralized planner that builds dispersive trees of forward‑propagated commands for each robot and negotiates shared space via column generation. By extending single‑robot dispersive‑tree search to multi‑robot teams and using asynchronous receding‑horizon loops, it reaches near‑optimal agreements in real time. The authors demonstrate significant travel‑time reductions and higher success rates on six‑robot hardware tests compared to existing planners.

### The Caveats
The near‑optimal coordination claim is unsubstantiated for larger teams, as the work evaluates only up to six robots and does not test scalability or communication‑delay robustness.

## OpenTac: Open‑Source 3D Tactile Skin Ecosystem

### The Breakthrough
OpenTac delivers a full‑stack 3D tactile skin that converts tangential loads into spatial pressure patterns while a common‑mode response measures normal force. An automated CAD tool generates fabrication files from 2‑D outlines or text, and the acquisition system reads partial taxel subsets at kilohertz rates—19.2× faster than full‑array raster scanning for a 1024‑taxel skin. The team released designs and software and showcased the skins on four real robots for contact‑rich manipulation tasks.

### The Caveats
The paper provides no quantitative comparison to existing tactile sensors or standard benchmarks, leaving its claimed performance and advantages unsubstantiated.

## Live‑Stream Tele‑Operation of a $4k 7‑DOF Robot

### The Breakthrough
A livestream system streams real‑time video from a $4,000, 7‑degree‑of‑freedom robot and exposes a web‑based interface that sends user commands directly to the robot controller. This architecture demonstrates low‑cost, accessible remote manipulation, bridging the gap between high‑end lab rigs and consumer‑grade hardware.

### The Caveats
The demo offers only a showcase video with no latency measurements, task success rates, safety checks, or multi‑user testing, so its practical teleoperation performance is unverified.

## DiffDreamer: World‑Model + Differentiable Simulation for Quadrotor Control

### The Breakthrough
DiffDreamer combines a learned latent world model with a differentiable physics simulator, allowing gradients to flow through the simulator while training a quadrotor controller. The actor loss blends critic‑driven rewards for nondifferentiable tasks and simulator‑driven rewards for differentiable motion objectives, speeding up learning for aggressive gate‑racing and dynamic‑tracking benchmarks.

### The Caveats
The reported gains rely on simulation and a single proof‑of‑concept quadrotor flight, with no extensive real‑world testing across multiple platforms or varied conditions.

## RoboJev: Video‑Based Robot Task Success Grader

### The Breakthrough
RoboJev fine‑tunes the 27B‑parameter vision‑language model JEV with LoRA on 52,598 robot episodes, using just ten sampled frames plus final views to output a success probability. It attains confidence scores up to 0.995 for successful attempts and AUROC around 0.89–0.90 on held‑out video benchmarks, promising automatic grading of large robot fleets.

### The Caveats
The system is only evaluated on offline video benchmarks and never tested on a live robot, so its claim to reliably grade real‑world robot fleets is unproven.

## Humanoid Mobility via Attention‑Based Contacts

### The Breakthrough
The paper introduces a self‑supervised attention‑based contact planner that predicts future foot‑environment contacts and a contact‑conditioned tracker that converts these plans into whole‑body motions, enabling onboard perception‑driven locomotion without reference trajectories.

### The Caveats
The paper presents no benchmark or hardware results and does not compare against any baselines, so the claimed versatile humanoid mobility remains unverified.

## Cerebras Trillion‑Parameter Model Deployment on Wafer‑Scale Chips

### The Breakthrough
Cerebras stores entire 16 GB layers of trillion‑parameter language models on individual wafers, keeping weights resident in on‑chip SRAM and passing only activations via RDMA (~2 µs per hop). By chaining up to 59 wafers, the system claims 1,000–2,000 tokens per second throughput with high request concurrency.

### The Caveats
The claimed throughput is unsupported, as no empirical hardware measurements or comparisons to existing baselines are presented.

## Junior: Local AI Engineer for macOS DevOps

### The Breakthrough
Junior bundles a large‑language‑model‑driven planner with native integrations to Linear, Slack, GitHub, and other dev tools, enabling it to fetch tickets, run CI diagnostics, and submit PR updates entirely on the user’s Mac, preserving privacy while demonstrating end‑to‑end autonomous software‑engineering tasks.

### The Caveats
Without formal evaluation or comparison to existing automation tools, it is unclear whether Junior actually outperforms simpler scripts or current CI assistants.

## Awesome‑CUA: Catalog of Computer‑Use Agents and Resources

### The Breakthrough
Awesome‑CUA aggregates 3,260 records—including 1,671 curated items and 2,789 papers/surveys—into a version‑controlled JSONL/SQLite catalog with daily automated scans and query scripts, offering ready‑to‑use RAG documents for language‑model agents.

### The Caveats
The claim of comprehensive coverage is unsubstantiated, as the repository provides no empirical validation of catalog completeness or usefulness.

### Priority
WarpWeaver delivers the most concrete real‑world multi‑robot results, showing near‑optimal coordination on actual hardware—a rare, actionable advance for embodied AI labs.

### One action
Clone the WarpWeaver code, run the provided six‑robot benchmark, and compare its travel‑time reductions to your current planner.

### What to watch
Hardware‑centric demos this week span coordination (WarpWeaver), sensing (OpenTac), and teleoperation (live‑stream robot). Together they illustrate a trend toward open, reproducible robot platforms that blend algorithmic novelty with tangible hardware deployments.
